issues.legal_issue: An agency created for valuable consideration to protect the agent’s interest in the subject matter cannot be terminated to the prejudice of that interest.
material_facts: The debtor gave the bank authority to execute a decree and collect the amounts due under it, with the proceeds to be credited to his account with the bank.
The debtor was indebted to the bank, and the power of attorney described the authority as irrevocable.
issues.conclusion: The power of attorney was coupled with the bank’s interest and could not be revoked to the prejudice of that interest.
issues.legal_principle: Section 202 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 provides that, where an agent has an interest in the property forming the subject matter of the agency, the agency cannot, absent an express contract, be terminated to the prejudice of that interest. An agency created for valuable consideration to effectuate security or secure the agent’s interest is not revocable to that prejudice.

predicates.execution_dispute: The parties are disputing the continuation of authority used in a decree-execution proceeding.
predicates.agent_has_interest_in_agency_subject_mat: The agent has an interest in the property or fund that is the subject matter of the agency.
predicates.authority_given_to_protect_that_interest: The principal gave the agent authority to deal with that property or fund to secure or satisfy the agent’s interest.

issues.definition: When an execution dispute concerns authority over a fund in which the agent has an interest, and the authority was given to protect that interest, the authority cannot be terminated to the prejudice of the agent’s interest.

issues.legal_issue: A direction to realise a specifically designated fund and apply it toward a debt can create an equitable assignment of that fund even without a legal transfer of the underlying decree.
material_facts: The power of attorney directed that amounts recovered under the decree be credited to the debtor’s account with the bank.
The decree proceeds were specifically earmarked to discharge the debt owed to the bank, and the bank was authorised to realise those proceeds and set them off against the debt.
The document contained no words transferring the decree, and it described the bank as acting on the debtor’s behalf.
issues.conclusion: The document did not legally transfer the decree, but it effected an equitable assignment of the decree proceeds to the extent necessary to discharge the debt owed to the bank.
issues.legal_principle: A direction or engagement to pay a creditor out of a particular fund can amount in equity to an assignment of so much of the fund as is needed to discharge the debt. The Court relied on Watson v. Duke of Wellington, (1830) 39 E.R. 231; Burn v. Carvalho, (1839) 41 E.R. 265; Jaga bhai Lallubhai v. Rustamji Nasarwanji, (1885) I.L.R. 9 Bom. 311; and Prahlad Pd. Modi v. Tikaiini Faldani Kumari. Because the document contained no words of transfer and left ownership of the decree proceeds with the debtor, there was no legal assignment.

predicates.debt_owed_to_agent: The person entitled to the fund owes a debt to the person authorised to receive or apply it.
predicates.particular_fund_identified_for_debt_paym: A particular fund is designated for payment of the debt.
predicates.agent_authorized_to_realize_fund_and_app: The creditor or its agent is authorised to realise the designated fund and apply the proceeds to the debt.

issues.definition: When a debtor owes a creditor and designates a particular fund for that debt, authorising the creditor to realise and apply the fund, the fund is equitably assigned to the extent of the debt.

issues.legal_issue: An equitable assignee who cannot use the procedure for a formal transfer of a decree may execute it under the procedural provision allowing proceedings by a person claiming under the decree-holder.
material_facts: The bank held an equitable assignment of the decree proceeds to the extent of the debtor’s debt to it.
The bank could not obtain the benefit of the procedure for execution by a transferee of a formally transferred decree.
The decree-holder objected to the bank proceeding with execution.
issues.conclusion: The bank could execute the decree in its own right under Section 146 of the Code of Civil Procedure despite being unable to proceed under Order XXI, Rule 16.
issues.legal_principle: In Jugalkishore Saraf v. Raw Cotton Co. Ltd., this Court held that an equitable assignee of a decree who cannot obtain the benefit of Order XXI, Rule 16 of the Code of Civil Procedure may nevertheless execute the decree under Section 146 of the Code. The Court followed that binding decision and found no compelling reason to reconsider it.

predicates.decree_execution_proceeding: The proceeding is for execution of a decree.
predicates.equitable_assignee_of_decree: A person has an equitable assignment of the decree or its proceeds.
predicates.formal_transferee_procedure_unavailable: The equitable assignee cannot use the procedure available to a transferee of a formally transferred decree.

issues.definition: In a decree-execution proceeding, an equitable assignee who cannot use the formal-transferee procedure may execute the decree through the procedure for a person claiming under the decree-holder.

issues.legal_issue: An execution application filed in the decree-holder’s name may continue for the equitable assignee where its original form followed the parties’ arrangement and the dispute arose only after filing.
material_facts: The bank initially filed the execution application in the decree-holder’s name, with the bank manager signing as attorney under the power of attorney.
There was no dispute between the debtor and the bank when the application was filed, and the form of the application followed the power of attorney.
The dispute arose while execution was pending, after which the bank asserted its own rights as equitable assignee.
issues.conclusion: The application could continue, and its form did not prevent the bank from executing the decree in its own right.
issues.legal_principle: The Court looked to the substance of the execution rather than its form. Since the application was filed in the decree-holder’s name as required by the power of attorney before any dispute arose, it served no useful purpose to close it; the bank could continue it in its own right as equitable assignee.

rule.if: decree_execution_proceeding and application_filed_in_decree_holder_name_under_authority and no_dispute_when_application_filed and dispute_arose_while_execution_pending and equitable_assignee_may_execute

predicates.decree_execution_proceeding: The proceeding is for execution of a decree.
predicates.application_filed_in_decree_holder_name_: The application was filed in the decree-holder’s name in accordance with authority given to the applicant or its agent.
predicates.no_dispute_when_application_filed: The decree-holder and the person acting under the authority were not in dispute when the application was filed.
predicates.dispute_arose_while_execution_pending: The dispute between the decree-holder and the person claiming an interest arose after the execution application was filed and while it remained pending.
predicates.equitable_assignee_may_execute: The person claiming to continue execution has an equitable assignment and may execute the decree in its own right.

issues.definition: Where an authorised application is filed in the decree-holder’s name before a dispute arises, and the claimant is entitled to execute as an equitable assignee, the pending application may continue for that claimant.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court cannot reject a pure legal contention going to the root of the matter solely because it was not pleaded or raised before the lower court.
material_facts: In the appeal from the execution order, the appellant argued that the bank had no right to execute without a transfer or assignment of the decree and that the execution court lacked jurisdiction.
The appellate court declined to consider the contention as a new point that had not been raised before the executing court.
The Supreme Court characterised the contention as a pure question of law going to the root of the matter.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court was not right to brush aside the pure legal contentions on the ground that they had not been pleaded or urged before the executing court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that pure legal contentions which, if valid, go to the root of the matter should not be rejected by an appellate court merely because they were not included in the pleadings or raised before the lower court. No earlier case or statutory provision was cited for this holding.

predicates.appeal_from_execution_order: The proceeding is an appeal from an order made in a decree-execution proceeding.
predicates.pure_legal_contention_goes_to_root: A party raises a pure question of law which, if valid, would affect the root of the matter.
predicates.appellate_court_rejects_it_only_because_: The appellate court refuses to consider the contention solely because it was not pleaded or raised before the lower court.

issues.definition: In an appeal from an execution order, an appellate court must consider a pure legal contention going to the root of the matter when it rejects that contention only because it was not raised below.
